'''Albert Llovera Massana'''{{family name footnote|lang=Catalan|Llovera|Massana}} (born 11 September 1966) is a [[rallying|rally]] driver and former [[alpine skiing|alpine skier]] from [[Andorra]]. He became the youngest athlete to compete in the [[Winter Olympics]] in 1984 at the age of 17.<ref name="SportsRef">{{cite Sports-Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ll/albert-llovera-1.html |title=Albert Llovera |access-date=20 March 2018 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418080625/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ll/albert-llovera-1.html |archive-date=18 April 2020 |quote=Full name: Albert Llovera Massana}}</ref> A serious accident in 1985 left him paralysed from the waist down. He has since taken up rallying, using cars with specially adapted hand controls. He is currently competing in the [[Super 2000 World Rally Championship]].

==Career==
[[File:Rally Finland 2010 - EK 1 - Albert Llovera.jpg|thumb|Llovera during [[2010 Rally Finland]].]]
At the age of 17, Llovera became the youngest ever athlete to compete in the [[Winter Olympics]] when he represented Andorra at the [[1984 Winter Olympics|1984 games]] in [[Sarajevo]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.albertllovera.com/en/albert-llovera/piloto |title=Driver |work=albertllovera.com |accessdate=20 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327231314/http://www.albertllovera.com/en/albert-llovera/piloto |archivedate=27 March 2012}}</ref> In the following year, 1985, whilst competing in the European Ski Cup, also in Sarajevo, he suffered a serious accident which left him using a wheelchair with [[paraplegia]] beginning at lower back level.

Llovera turned to motorsport, first competing on [[quad bikes]] and then starting in rallying. In 1989, he won the Peugeot Rally Cup in Andorra. In 2001, with the support of [[Fiat]], he began competing in the [[Junior World Rally Championship]] in a [[Fiat Punto S1600]]. He continued in the championship in 2002.

After competing in Spain along with selected WRC appearances, Llovera returned full-time to the world stage in 2010 to contest the [[Super 2000 World Rally Championship]] in a [[Fiat Abarth Grande Punto S2000]]. He finished fifth in class on his first event [[2010 Rally Mexico|Rally Mexico]]. He scored a best overall result of 17th on [[2010 Rally Catalunya|Rally Catalunya]], which was not a round of the SWRC.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ewrc-results.com/profile.php?profile=274 |title=Driver profile - Albert Llovera |work=eWRC-results.com |publisher=eWRC.cz |accessdate=20 July 2011}}</ref>

Llovera continued in the SWRC in 2011, finishing fourth in the category in [[2011 Jordan Rally|Jordan]].

In 2020, Llovera competed in the Dakar rally in an Iveco truck from the Dutch Team de Rooy.
